description:
Boot-time reporter called by the orchestrator at startup. Returns independent top-level fields that the orchestrator must branch on separately:

**`outdated` (array of stale artifact keys) — soft notification.**
Compares the host's `.aide/versions.json` against the canonical manifest shipped with this running server — never against the latest published version, so files that match the version the project runs are current even when a newer release exists. Each element names an artifact key that is behind. An empty array means everything is current. A missing `.aide/versions.json` (old install predating version tracking) silently collapses to `[]`. Staleness is informational — the orchestrator continues with a heads-up to the user.

**`behind` (`{ installed, latest, launch, versionsBehind, highlights }` or null) — soft notification.** Non-null when the running server is older than the latest published version, whatever launch the project's `aide` entry uses — a global install or npx, pinned or not. `installed` is the running server's version. `launch` (`global` or `local`) picks the remedy: `global` → `npm i -g @aidemd-mcp/server@{latest}`; `local` → first install `latest` into the npx cache, then move the project's aide pin to it with `aide_upgrade({ category: "mcp", targetVersion: latest })`, never a hand edit of `.mcp.json`; if the install fails, switch nothing; once the newer server runs, `/aide:upgrade` offers to switch the entry to the global command. `versionsBehind` (1 or more) counts the published releases after `installed` up to `latest`; `highlights` holds 0–3 one-line notes of what they added or fixed (empty when the release notes were unavailable). Show the count and highlights briefly, never the changelog. Either upgrade takes effect only in a new session. It never gates the pipeline. Null when there is no `aide` entry, the running version is unknown, the server is current, or the version check could not run (offline checks pass silently).

**`brainMigration` (`{ staleSections, legacyLauncher }` or null) — soft notification.** Non-null when the brain config has sections whose text matches an earlier template version, or a legacy brain launcher (`legacyLauncher` lists the reasons: npx-launch, unpinned, unversioned, older-pin, missing-auto-confirm). Mention it once and suggest `/aide:brain config`; it never gates the pipeline and never changes `brain.status`.

**`brain` (precondition state) — hard gate.**
Reports whether the host's brain MCP entry is wired and consistent. Shape: `{ status, name?, fault?, hints }` — `name` is absent on `no-brain-aide` and `brain-aide-invalid`; `fault` is present only on `brain-aide-invalid`. The orchestrator must halt and direct the user to resolve the issue before continuing if `status` is not `'ok'`. No path validation is performed — the package never stats any directory on disk; state derives entirely from comparing `.aide/config/brain.aide` against `.mcp.json`.

The five `brain.status` values:
- `ok` — `.aide/config/brain.aide` exists, satisfies the required-section contract, and the host's `.mcp.json` `brain` entry matches the parsed `mcpServerConfig`. `name` is the user-declared descriptive label from brain.aide. The pipeline may proceed.
- `no-brain-aide` — `.aide/config/brain.aide` is absent. No `name` field. Remediation: run `/aide:brain config`, which creates the config.
- `brain-aide-invalid` — the file exists but falls short. `fault.kind` is `missing-sections` (with `fault.sections` naming each missing required section) or `malformed` (with `fault.reason`). No `name` field. Remediation: run `/aide:brain config`.
- `no-mcp-entry` — brain.aide parsed successfully but the host's `.mcp.json` is absent, malformed, or has no `mcpServers.brain` key. `name` is present. Remediation: run sync with the same launcher the project's `aide` MCP entry uses — `aidemd-mcp sync` when the project's `aide` MCP entry runs the globally installed `aidemd-mcp`, or `npx -y @aidemd-mcp/server@<version> sync` with the version that entry pins when it runs through npx.
- `mcp-drift` — brain.aide and `.mcp.json` both exist but their `brain` entries disagree on `command` or `args`. `name` is present. Remediation: run sync with the same launcher the project's `aide` MCP entry uses — `aidemd-mcp sync` when the project's `aide` MCP entry runs the globally installed `aidemd-mcp`, or `npx -y @aidemd-mcp/server@<version> sync` with the version that entry pins when it runs through npx.

`hints` is always present on every status — an array of candidate brain root paths the orchestrator can surface during recovery.

No parameters needed — uses the server's working directory.
name: aide_info
